title: The Pastoral Office is Covenantal in Nature
speaker: Pastor Renan Pereira
summary: Pastor Renan Pereira explains the biblical nature of the pastoral office as a covenantal ministry essential to the church's health and function. Drawing from 1 Timothy 3:14-16 and Paul's instructions to Timothy in Ephesus, he addresses why pastors must maintain biblical standards despite opposition, how godliness and faithfulness characterize true pastoral leadership, and the congregation's responsibility to support and honor their pastors.

outline.title: The Context of 1 Timothy: Paul's Love for Ephesus and Timothy's Ministry
subpoints: Paul's deep affection for the Ephesian church and his emotional departure from them
Timothy's arrival as pastor to address heresies, Judaizers, and various conflicts in the church
Paul's letter provides specific instructions for maintaining order in God's house despite Timothy's youth and the opposition he faced

outline.title: Five Reasons for Understanding the Pastoral Office
subpoints: The author's own pastoral tensions, crises, and conflicts requiring biblical solutions
The need for repetition: Timothy and the church needed to hear Paul's instructions repeatedly for reinforcement and public support
The importance of clear distinctions in the church between those to be rejected and those to be accepted
Responding to contemporary books on spiritual abuse by establishing proper biblical understanding of pastoral function
General ignorance among church members, leaders, pastors, elders, and deacons about the actual function and role of the pastoral office

outline.title: Paul's Counsel to Timothy: Four Essential Lessons
subpoints: Paul re-established the biblical standard for the pastoral office rather than offering pragmatic compromise
Pastors must be examples in godliness and faithfulness, never retreating despite opposition; they bear the yoke with two sides—faithfulness and godliness

Mature biblical teaching on conduct in God's house must be taught repeatedly in season and out of season, including qualifications of officers, the nature of the church's mission, and Christ as head and king
Never underestimate contentious and unsubmissive people who love preeminence and strange doctrines; disorder in leadership produces disorder in the congregation

outline.title: The Essential Functions and Authority of the Pastoral Office
subpoints: Pastors teach, govern, rebuke, correct, train, mediate conflicts, and counsel the congregation
The pastoral office serves as a covenantal, mediating ministry essential to church health
Good pastors are a sign of God's blessing; bad pastors are a sign of God's judgment
The church is not a democracy but a monarchy with Christ as king, pastors as ambassadors, and the Bible as constitution

outline.title: Responsibilities of the Congregation Toward Their Pastors
subpoints: Support, encourage, strengthen, and uphold the pastor God has placed among you so he can lead without groaning
Honor pastors through obedience to the Lord, imitation of their virtues, submission to their lawful commands and corrections
Bear with pastoral infirmities and cover them in love
Pray for the pastor and his family continually; recognize that whatever strikes the shepherd affects the flock
Prayer for the pastor is fundamental to his remaining faithful and godly

outline.title: Responsibilities of Church Elders and Officers
subpoints: Never treat the flock as though it belongs to you; carry out ministry according to Christ's purpose and manner
Maintain biblical doctrine and order established by Christ
Do not retreat from or exceed what Christ has commanded; be faithful and diligent
Laziness and complacency in church office are sins
Cultivate an eschatological vision, looking to eternity and remembering you will give account to the Lord for your ministry

transcript:
## Scripture Reading

> "These things I write to you, though I hope to come to you shortly. But if I am delayed, I write so that you may know how you ought to conduct yourselves in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. And without controversy, great is the mystery of godliness. God was manifested in the flesh, justified in the spirit, seen by angels, preached among the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up in glory." (1 Timothy 3:14-16)

## Introduction

Good morning, brothers. I had the purpose of writing down exactly what I was going to preach to help my brother, Pastor Tito. But I think that's just a little bit of excuse for myself. Because I've never spent so much time without preaching. For the last 20 years I've preached three times on average every Sunday. And it's been almost six months since I preached. This is a great time for me to learn more and to also just be able to sit and learn from other pastors. And there is a relationship between what I'm going to preach here today and this time that I've been here with you to learn more.

Today we want to talk about the office of the pastor, the office of the minister as a covenantal office in the church.

## The Historical Context of 1 Timothy

Let me spend a couple of minutes bringing into context what was read from the word this morning. Paul wrote the letter that had been sent to him to solve problems in the church of Ephesus. According to some theologians, this is the church most loved by Paul. Some scholars believe that Ephesus was the most beloved church by Paul. He spent a lot of time there and had a great ministry with great success there. But something changed once Paul departed. He had to say goodbye to the church in a very emotional moment.

This great love and affection that Paul has for the Ephesian church is really well seen in the letter to the Ephesians, where Paul says that they are not to be sad, upset, or mourn over the fact that he is in jail on their behalf. The description of this in the original text is very strong. It was an extremely strong event, and the letter to the Ephesians confirms how difficult it was for the spirit of the church. The event that occurred in Acts 20 was very strong, and when you read the letter to the Ephesians, you have the feeling that this contributed negatively to the growth of the Ephesian church.

So then comes 1 Timothy, which comes later in history when Timothy is now a pastor of Ephesus, there to solve all kinds of problems. There are problems with heresies, problems with Judaizers coming to the church, and even more. But at the moment when he began to exercise his role as a pastor according to Paul's own order, the problems were not only in the general ministry in the church. They were no longer just mourning over Paul's absence or solving the problems of other churches. Now there were also attacks because Timothy fulfilled his role.

Somehow, Paul knew what was happening with Timothy in the church of Ephesus. We don't know exactly how Paul learned of what was going on, what the church was doing to Timothy. But what led Paul to write 1 Timothy to help him is what is described in the passage we read today, 1 Timothy 3:14-15.

When Timothy was there, Paul knew about these battles and these battles needed specific instructions on how to solve the problems of the church of Ephesus. And these problems should be solved with the maintenance of order, the way it should proceed in the house of God. Verse 16 is the motivational instrument that Paul uses to prevent Timothy from being humiliated by the maintenance of order. Just as the Lord Jesus Christ was sent to the heavens to fulfill the ministry here and fulfilled it with integrity, Timothy should be motivated. Even though he was being humiliated, as Jesus was humiliated, to fully fulfill the ministry that was designated to him. In the order of God, Timothy was also sent with the same purpose. In the same way that Christ was humiliated as the minister of God, Timothy is being humiliated and he needs to persevere in that ministry.

This is what I've been writing about in the last six months. And I don't want to return to Brazil without sharing what the scriptures teach us about the importance of cultivating the pastoral office in the life of the local church.

## Why This Subject Matters: Five Reasons

### Reason One: My Own Pastoral Struggles

I'd like to tell you a few reasons why I chose to write on this particular subject. The first reason I chose was my own questions, my own tensions, my own difficulties, my own dilemmas, my own conflicts as a pastor. A few years ago, I understood that the tensions, crises, and difficulties I faced as a pastor, husband, father, and as part of the church needed a specific and qualified response.

The majority of pastoral books talk about principles to solve the minister's crisis in a very generalized manner. I found basically two books that used the pastoral letters as a source of specific advice. So I decided to seek advice for myself and decided to start explaining this to the presbyters and deacons of my church. Realizing that this is something that should happen for myself and for others, I decided to start by actually explaining this first to the elders and deacons of my own church.

So for over a year, I preached through the three pastoral epistles of 1 Timothy, 2 Timothy, and Titus. Alongside this, I also provided several Sunday school lessons on the same subject. And then every fifteen days, I met with the elders and deacons, and we went through the Westminster Standards, the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church of Brazil, and the pastoral epistles on this subject. If the leaders didn't really buy into this idea, if they didn't understand the covenantal nature of the office of the pastor, telling the church wouldn't do anything because the leaders would not be on board.

### Reason Two: Why Paul Repeats His Instructions

The second reason I had to write this came from two questions that came to my mind. Why is it that Paul writes again to Timothy about matters that Timothy already knew and that the church in Ephesus already knew? Why write so that Timothy would know something he already is aware of?

It's very likely that Timothy actually witnessed and participated in the training of the elders in Ephesus and was even present at their ordination. So why repeat again if this is something Timothy already knew? The answer is that Timothy, just like all of us, needs repetition. We need to hear the same things over and over and over again. Timothy also needed the public support of Paul—that strong public support of Paul—that this letter would provide as it's read to the congregation. The opposition was very strong, even starting with the doubt as to whether he would be able to do what he's called to do because he was so young.

A very famous commentator called Moo says that the presbyters were involved with these conflicts. Moo, a New Testament scholar, even says that he thinks that the elders were involved in this antagonism towards Timothy.

Another reason why Paul repeats what he already said is to bring segregation in the church. It's evident who were the approved ones of the community. This would be a great help to the pastor's work. It would help Timothy quite a bit in exercising his office as a pastor if it was clear those who are to be rejected and those that have to be accepted.

### Reason Three: Addressing the Culture of Spiritual Abuse

Another reason why I decided to write on this is the popularity of two books discussing the supposed culture of spiritual abuse. One by Michael Kruger and the other by Scott McKnight. These two books are about the idea of spiritual abuse supposedly done by pastors. I know of a few cases of a pastor who was removed from his church without any proof because of the book of Scott McKnight.

There are two things that can be said about this. The first one is that these books recognize the conflicts that exist because of unknowing biblical knowledge about the pastor's function. This is the first reason. The second is that the solution presented was the most deleterious, the most dangerous, the most destructive that I could have read in a book. The book encourages the denunciation against pastors without proof. It encourages that accusation against pastors be taken at face value without any proof brought against the pastor.

So is this a solution or is it a problem? And I guarantee you, after years of study, that weakening the pastor's office is an even greater problem than creating a system to punish pastors without due diligence in following the scriptures. The solution is not just to say that every pastor abuses their congregation or every pastor is potentially an abuser. The solution is actually to have a well-defined vision of the office of the minister, instead of just putting every pastor in the same bag and saying that everybody is an abuser.

### Reason Four: Understanding of the Pastoral Office

One last reason that led me to write on this subject is that I was already a member of the church. I was a member of a church once. And in my experience as a member of church, people in general, including the leaders of the church, don't really know what the function of the pastor is. What happens is that people just decide to arbitrarily add things to what it means to be a pastor or to take things away from what it means to be a pastor without necessarily considering the Bible. And this just deepens the problems in the church.

Secondly, I have been a pastor for the last twenty years in large churches. And unfortunately, even the pastors don't know what their office is, what they are supposed to do as pastors. For some reason, God put me in the condition to advise pastors. And they don't really know how to put the role they should develop in the church in their place. And even they don't know what they are calling, what God calls them in the word to do in the church. And alongside that, even the elders and deacons don't understand it either. And because of that, in some cases, there is negligence in leading the church.

Nobody should do any work without understanding what the pastor's office is, what the pastor's function is. And that led me to conclude that no one should be an officer in the church, either pastor, deacon, or elder, if they don't understand what it means to be a pastor, what the office of the pastor is according to the scriptures. Especially the session of the church, because it is where the focus is, or where the focus of the church is diluted because of uncertainty about the pastor's function. The session is where the teaching of the church comes from, but also where problems are brought to by the congregation that may not know what the function of the pastor is.

So I wanted to share with you what I learned in the last few months, especially what I learned for myself personally, for my family, for my church.

## Key Lessons About Pastoral Ministry

### Lesson One: Ministerial Conflicts Are Ancient and Require Biblical Solutions

I've learned that ministerial conflicts are as old as the church itself. So this problem of ordering the church is as old as the church itself. And the solution that the Bible presents is as old as the church itself as well. Timothy was despised because of his youth; he suffered personal attacks. You know what an attack against a pastor is, don't you? Do you think there is a biblical foundation for such attacks? Often the accusation against a pastor is that, oh, he moves his arm in a funny way, or he moves his arms too fast in preaching, and that's not what a pastor should do. Should a pastor be disqualified from the office by using a standard that's not what God gave to us in his word?

Timothy found himself in the midst of doctrinal, liturgical, and ecclesiastic conflicts. So what was the solution that Paul offered him? Do you think it is as obvious to us today as it was to Paul and Timothy?

How did Paul answer first? Paul reminded Timothy and re-established the biblical standard for the pastor's office so that proper conduct in God's house would be maintained. Paul also rejected any expectations that fell outside of the biblical standard. And Paul also required that the minister fulfill the office faithfully, completely, without negligence, without fear, and without cowardice.

Notice that Paul did not give Timothy pragmatic counsel. He didn't say, Timothy, just don't do what God calls you to do as a servant of the church. Paul didn't say, you know what, you're facing so much trouble doing the things I asked you to do, doing the things the Bible calls you to do. Why don't you just step back from a few of those things, compromise with the different parties in the church, and just let's all get along? Without taking what the Bible says concerning the office of the pastor, the conflicts, the tensions, and the opposition would have remained at a high level instead of having been addressed from the word.

### Lesson Two: Pastors Must Be Examples in Godliness and Faithfulness

Rather than retreating, pastors must be examples in two areas: godliness and faithfulness. Paul tells Timothy, don't let anybody despise your youth; rather, become a pattern for the faithful. Don't retreat, keep the pattern, keep the standard. And those who are called to the office of the pastor have been gifted by God to lead the church in these two areas.

If there's somebody that you're considering for the ministry and they're not characterized by faithfulness and godliness, don't ordain them to the office, don't even consider them for the office.

In the Seara, where I am, people used to use donkeys. They would put a cane on top of the donkey to carry heavy things. And they would put a yoke on top of the donkey to carry very heavy things on either side of the donkey. And if you just put stuff on one side of the donkey, the whole yoke would flip over, and sometimes the donkey would flip over.

In the same way, and I don't know if I like this comparison, but in the same way as a donkey, the pastor has a yoke on him, and the two sides of that yoke are faithfulness and godliness. Pastors are gifted by God to carry these virtues to Jesus.

### Lesson Three: Mature Biblical Teaching Must Be Reiterated Continually

The third thing I learned was that the teaching of the mature, of those things that are the norm of how you should proceed in the house of God, should be reentered insistently at time and out of time. Mature teaching concerning the biblical norm for conduct in God's household must be repeated continually in season and out of season.

First, you should never forget what the qualifications and duties of both the elders and the deacons are in a church. The nature, the authority, the limits, and the responsibility of their offices must be continually brought before the church.

Secondly, the nature and the mission of the church must be taught repeatedly to the local church. Church leaders should be seen as those that are guiding the church towards the goal, the mission, the reason why God gave her to exist.

Third, within what Paul says should be taught, Christ is the head and king of the church. Therefore, both church officers and the congregation must understand that they are obligated to do what Christ has willed, commanded, and revealed in His word. This is fundamental, essential, and determinative.

### Lesson Four: Never Underestimate Contentious and Unsubmissive People

The fourth and last thing that I learned: Never underestimate contentious and unsubmissive people. What is the specialty of these people? They like to have the preeminence. They don't like serving just in the backstage to be only seen later. They want to sit in a place that is right next to the window. If you love the preeminence, you always want to sit at the window.

These contentious and unsubmissive people, they love the preeminence in the church. But also, they love strange doctrines. They love novelty. They love different things. They also like contentious people. Because of the question of the doctrines, they always like to debate. This always generates alternative and singular thoughts. This always leads to division because you have a bunch of individual singular thoughts instead of a cohesive doctrine.

I've learned in my life as a pastor that disillusioned or disorderly minds also produce disorder in the church. There's only one way of doing things in the house of God, not several ways. People who are contentious and unsubmissive often have all kinds of ways that are supposed to be done, not just the way of Christ. This is true of both pastors and the sheep.

## The Essential Nature of the Pastoral Office

The pastoral office is essential to the church. Pastors teach, they govern, they rebuke, they correct, they train, they mediate conflicts, they counsel, and much more. Experience a church, or being in a church without a pastor, or in a church with a bad pastor, and you will quickly realize how profoundly the pastoral office serves as a covenantal, mediating ministry.

Jesus promised us that he would give us pastors, and he did that in the Old Testament. And Paul told the Ephesians, who were having trouble submitting to the pastor, that Christ, Jesus, gives pastors to the church.

## Application to the Congregation

### First Application: Seeking Good Pastors from Christ

So if you want a faithful pastor, pray to the one who is the only one who can give and maintain faithful pastors to the church. Good pastors are the sign of the blessing of God, and bad pastors are the sign of the judgment of God.

### Second Application: Don't Create Your Own Ecclesiastical Ways

Second thing: don't create your own ways of doing things in the local church. Don't create a particular ecclesiology; don't legislate; don't establish a mission and proposal to the church on your own. Choose officers—elders, deacons, pastors—who know that Christ is the head of the church, not themselves, but Christ in His Word.

Just this little note here: the church is not a democracy. The church is a monarchy in which Christ is the king, the pastors are the ambassadors, and the Bible is a constitution. If an ambassador ever spoke something that the king did not give him to speak, or did something that the king did not order him to do, he would be executed. So it is of utmost importance that the officers of the church are committed to the king and his kingdom.

### Third Application: Learn About and Support Your Pastor

Learn about the pastoral office so that you may support, encourage, strengthen, and uphold the pastor whom God has placed among you. It's important that he is able to lead you without groaning. His groaning, not your groaning. If he serves with grief, it will be a great blessing for the church. If he serves without grief, it will be a great blessing for the church, for him to be able to lead you without groaning. If he serves with grief, it will benefit neither the church, nor himself, nor his family. Hebrews 13:17 tells us that.

> "Honor the pastors with obedience to the Lord, because it is a long life happiness. The imitation of their virtues and graces, will in obedience to their lawful commands and counsels, do submission to their corrections, fidelity to the defense and maintenance of their persons and authority, according to their several ranks and the nature of their places, bearing with their infirmities and covering them in love that so they may be an honor to them and to their government." (Westminster Shorter Catechism, Question 127)

This question from the catechism makes something very clear: Never, never treat a true shepherd the way you treat a false shepherd, nor treat a false shepherd the way that you treat a true shepherd.

### Fourth Application: Pray for Your Pastor

And then one last application: Pray for him. Pray and remember the end of question 127. Bearing with their infirmities and covering them in love that so they may be an honor to them and to their government.

Without the comprehension that prayer for the pastor is fundamental for him to stay firm and godly, you will suffer. Whatever strikes the shepherd affects the flock in some measure. If you want the good of the church, you want the good of your pastor and his family. If you want the good of the church, pray for his family.

It is because your prayer for your pastor is fundamental so that he can stay faithful and godly, you must pray. Whatever strikes the shepherd affects the flock in some measure.

## Application to Church Officers

Now I address the elders of this church. Pastors, elders: never treat the flock as though it belonged to you. Carry out your ministry according to Christ's purpose and in Christ's appointed manner. This will produce peace, unity, and purity within the flock as fruits of the faithful exercise of pastoral functions.

Maintain a standard of doctrine. Maintain the order established by Christ, because governing as Christ wants is the same as Christ governing. Neither retreat nor go beyond what Christ has commanded; be faithful. Whoever cannot be diligent should not hold church office. Laziness and complacency are sins.

Whoever is an activist governs distrusting the efficacy of the head. Cultivate an eschatological vision, looking to eternity. Know that you will give an account for your ministry to the Lord. Elders, cultivate an eschatological, an eternal view to your ministry. Look forward to eternity, knowing that one day you're going to give an account for your ministry to the Lord of the Church.

God bless you, and we're very happy that my family and I were able to be with you during this time.
